components: Write-through cache: requests or updates an item
Write-through cache: holds process-local hot data

steps: A caller submits v4 through the cache interface.
The cache records or reserves the new version.
The backing store synchronously persists v4.
Success is returned only after the write-through policy completes both paths.

lesson.scenario: A pricing API writes a new price through a cache tier that synchronously updates durable storage.

steps.title: Version 17
steps.narration: Cache and database both store price 25 at version 17.
steps.outcome: Reads are aligned before the write.
steps.invariant: The source remains authoritative even when writes enter through the cache.

steps.title: Write enters cache
steps.narration: The API sends version 18 and waits for synchronous completion.
steps.outcome: The cache must not acknowledge an unpersisted value.
steps.invariant: Write-through success requires the configured durable source write.

steps.title: Database commits
steps.narration: The cache persists version 18 in the pricing database.
steps.outcome: The authoritative row now contains version 18.
steps.invariant: Source and cache writes need an explicit failure and retry policy.

steps.title: Cache publishes
steps.narration: After the durable acknowledgement, version 18 becomes readable.
steps.outcome: The client receives success only after both tiers agree.
steps.invariant: Readers must not observe the new cache value before the source commit when that is the promised contract.

steps.title: Reader hits new value
steps.narration: A reader obtains price 29 version 18 from the cache.
steps.outcome: The write cost buys an immediately warm cache.
steps.invariant: Every write pays cache coordination and source latency.
